key_idea: Encode a 'line rule' whose only solutions are built from the p-adic last-nonzero-digit function, which can have no vertical period. Express that rule as a finite system of tiling equations in Z^2 × Z/QZ, stack the system into one tile using a partition with full difference sets, and lift it rigidly to Z^3 and R^3 using residue transversals.
reason: Several of the individual moves are clever and short: the affine-approximation obstruction to periodicity, the stacking by a partition with full difference sets, the rigidity of residue transversals, and the volume-and-connectivity argument for grid centers. Still, the whole argument is a long reduction chain with many gadgets (channels, dependence, cycle and activation tiles), and the bookkeeping hides the single reason the result holds.
recognized: Follows the Greenfeld–Tao programme disproving the periodic tiling conjecture (p-adic line rule, stacking of tiling systems, lifting to Euclidean space), here pushed down to dimension 3
